# Platform Overview

## What It Is

Activepieces is an open-source workflow automation platform positioned as a
"Zapier alternative" [2]. It enables users to build automation flows connecting
business tools via a visual, step-based builder [21][22].

|-----------|-------|--------|

| YC Batch | Summer 2022 | [1] |
| Headquarters | San Francisco, CA | [1] |
| Primary Language | TypeScript | [4] |
| Backend Framework | Fastify (Node.js) | [4] |
| Frontend | React | [4] |
| Database | PostgreSQL (or PGLite for single-instance) | [4][8] |
| Queue | Redis + BullMQ | [4] |
| Monorepo Manager | Turbo | [4] |
| License | MIT (community) + Commercial (enterprise) | [3] |

### Architecture

The platform uses a queue-based, event-driven architecture [4]:

- **App**: Organizes APIs and scheduled jobs
- **Worker**: Polls job queues, allocates sandboxes, executes flows via engine
- **Sandbox**: Isolated execution environment managing process lifecycle
- **Engine**: TypeScript code that parses flow JSON and executes as compiled JS
- **UI**: React-based frontend

Workers and the app are stateless, enabling horizontal scaling [4]. Redis
(via BullMQ) handles job queuing capable of thousands of jobs per second [4].

## Licensing

### License Structure

Activepieces uses a dual-license "open core" model [3]:

| Component | License | Directories |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Core/Community | MIT (OSI-approved) | All except enterprise dirs | 
| Enterprise features | Commercial/Proprietary | `packages/ee/`, `packages/server/api/src/app/ee/` |

The MIT license permits use, modification, and redistribution for any purpose
including commercial use, with the only requirement being inclusion of the
license notice [3].

### Personal Use Implications

- Self-hosting the community edition is unrestricted under MIT [3]
- Enterprise features (RBAC, SSO, audit logging) require a commercial license [3]
- No task or execution limits on self-hosted community edition [22]
- Cannot upgrade from PGLite (single Docker) to Enterprise without migration [8]

### License vs n8n

| Aspect | Activepieces | n8n |
|--------|-------------|-----|
| License type | MIT (OSI-approved) | Sustainable Use License (not OSI) |
| Commercial use | Unrestricted | Cannot build competing hosted service |
| Fork rights | Full | Source-available but restricted |

This is a significant differentiator frequently cited in comparisons [21][22][23].

### Release Cadence

The Docker Compose file references version 0.80.1 [10], indicating active
development. Discovery agents reported weekly self-hosted releases (unverified
against official changelog).

### Notable Adoption

SOC 2 Type II certified [22]. Claims of usage by Google, Red Bull, Rakuten,
ClickUp were found in discovery but could not be verified against case studies.
Funding Societies is a documented enterprise customer.

### Market Positioning

Activepieces positions itself as "AI-first" automation with emphasis on MCP
integration [2][24]. The platform targets non-technical users and small teams,
differentiating from n8n's developer-focused approach [21][22].
